correctness.rationale: Step 1 reconstructs the exact pointwise integer-valued first return R=1+floor(BZ), including dyadic endpoints; conditioning on an independent Pareto B yields the all-integer tail formula. The induced stationary distribution and bounded density follow from the founding Theorem 3.1 and Lemma 3.1 at alpha=0. The layer-cake formula and exponential depth tail prove the sharp asymptotic and remainder. Dominated convergence gives the joint conditioned law, and tower normalization gives the if-and-only-if moment and finite-mass thresholds. A standalone rational and quadrature checker passed 834 supporting finite tests, not relied on for the infinite conclusions.

originality.rationale: The exact map-specific stationary tail and conditional size-biased depth/Pareto overshoot theorem were compared by implication, not title, with the complete founding arXiv preprint and related inducing sources. Proposition 4.6 gives shell-mass bounds, Remark 4.5 only the infinite-measure half, while the new result proves an exact first-return law, sharp quantitative remainder and joint conditional distribution. Searches for equivalent formulations and stronger coverage did not reveal such a statement. The later journal edition and some general texts are only partly accessible and are explicitly retained as residual risks.
residual_risks: An equivalent specialization may occur in the inaccessible portions of the revised 2024 journal article.
General inducing/renewal literature may already include the joint conditioned size-biased law in a framework applying directly to this example; current primary-source comparisons were not exhaustive.
The stationary constant is specified as an expectation over the induced measure, rather than evaluated in elementary closed form.

value.rationale: The exact law addresses the natural duration of excursions from the expanding section in a published wide-entrance intermittent model. It identifies a sharp dynamical tail and a new geometrically meaningful selection effect: long excursions size-bias the depth of the starting section point by a power of its logarithmic distance to the discontinuity. The if-and-only-if finite-measure boundary upgrades a previously one-sided result. This is more informative than a routine invariant-shell estimate, and can guide precise renewal/occupation calculations for this specific random system.
